newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-MOZAMBIQUE BEAT MALAWI TO REACH FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOZAMBIQUE BEAT MALAWI TO REACH FINALS.

text.p: Two goals in the last five minutes gave Mozambique a dramatic 2-1 win over Malawi on Saturday and a place in next year's African Nations' Cup finals.
Malawi needed a draw to qualify for only the second time in their history and looked on course when defender Manson Shabba Phiri stunned the hosts with a goal in the 62nd minute.
But Pinto Barros equalised five minutes from time and, roared on by a 35,000 crowd at the Machava Stadium, Mozambique pushed forward and striker Tico Tico hit the winner two minutes later.
The victory sent Mozambique to the 1998 tournament, the third time they have reached the finals after 1986 and 1996.
Zambia clinched the top spot in the group and their place in the finals with a 1-0 win over Mauritius in Lusaka.
Vincent Mutale scored just before halftime to give the injury-weakened Zambian side victory and ensure that Mauritius finished the six-match qualifying campaign in last place.
Hosts Burkina Faso, holders South Africa, Cameroon, Ghana, Guinea, Morocco, Togo and Tunisia have already qualified for the tournament which will be held next February.
The remaining six qualifying places will be decided on Sunday when nine other qualifiers are played around the continent.
